data.hypothesis: Increasing the source tile from 512 to 1024 while keeping a 128-thread CTA could halve the tile-loop and barrier count for the official large sizes. This raises dynamic shared memory from 8 KiB to 16 KiB and requires each thread to stage more records, so any synchronization savings may be offset by staging cost or occupancy. The controller must determine the result with its correctness suite and timing metric.

memory_lessons.applicability: This conventional tiling kernel uses a 128-thread CTA; the 1024-entry tile candidate tests whether reducing synchronization frequency beyond the previously measured 128- and 256-entry tiles helps.
memory_lessons.claim: The valid 128-thread/128-source configuration measured 0.0008997683 seconds, while the valid 128-thread/256-source configuration measured 0.0008920329 seconds. Their close means do not establish that larger tiles are generally faster.
memory_lessons.next_experiment: Compare this candidate against those measurements using the official correctness suite and timing metric; treat the 1024-entry result as unmeasured until the controller reports it.

data.notes: This is a source-tile-size experiment against the supplied 512-entry tile. The target block remains 128 threads with one target and accumulator per thread. The complete correctness suite and official timing remain for the controller to evaluate.
transformations: Increase the source tile to 1024 compact 16-byte particle records and reserve 16384 bytes of dynamic shared memory; keep the block and items_per_block at 128.

Preserve cooperative staging and zero-fill for partial tiles, both CTA-wide barriers, global-index self-interaction exclusion, active-target guarding, one output per valid thread, and the original integration expressions.
